providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a product is the sum, and for commutative group schemes a sum of homomorphisms induces the sum of the maps of co-Lie complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tensor formula for Lie complexes
providers.scope: For a group scheme over a diagram, the internal mixed Hom from its co-Lie complex into a bounded below complex is the derived tensor product with its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Torsors under a commutative group
providers.scope: The co-Lie complex of a torsor under a commutative group scheme G, over a scheme or a diagram of schemes, is the pullback of the co-Lie complex of G.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The adjoint co-Lie complex of a commutative group
providers.scope: For a commutative group scheme the adjoint co-Lie complex is the co-Lie complex with the trivial action.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of the nerve
providers.scope: The Lie complex of the nerve of a commutative group scheme is the nerve of its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of the spectrum
providers.scope: The Lie complex of the spectrum of a commutative group scheme is the spectrum of its Lie complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Second nerves on spectral pseudo-categories
providers.scope: On the pseudo-category of a graded action, the second nerve is fully faithful on bounded derived categories, with image the objects whose cohomology is cartesian along the maps fixing the first vertex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie complex of a module scheme
providers.scope: The Lie complex of a module scheme over a ring scheme A has a canonical structure of a complex over the derived tensor product of A and the structure ring, determined by the spectral nerve.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exact sequences of module schemes
providers.scope: An exact sequence of module schemes gives a distinguished triangle of their Lie complexes over the stable ring with coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Ext formula
providers.scope: The Ext groups of the cotangent complex of the spectral nerve of a module scheme are Ext groups of modules into its Lie complex with coefficients.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Relative Ext groups of the spectral nerve
providers.scope: Relative Ext groups of the cotangent complex for a homomorphism of module schemes are Ext groups of modules out of its cone.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of module schemes and of their spectral nerves
providers.scope: Deformations of a module scheme over a first-order thickening are the same as deformations of the morphism from its spectral nerve to that of the base.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of module schemes
providers.scope: A module scheme deforms exactly when an obstruction in Ext^2 of modules into its Lie complex tensored with the ideal vanishes; deformations then form a torsor under Ext^1, with automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending homomorphisms of module schemes
providers.scope: A homomorphism of module schemes extends to given deformations exactly when a class in Ext^1 vanishes; the extensions then form a torsor under Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a homomorphism of module schemes with a given target
providers.scope: Deformations of a module scheme together with an extension of a homomorphism to a given deformation of the target are classified by Ext groups of modules into the fibre of the map of Lie complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Two deformations of the target module scheme
providers.scope: For two deformations of the target, the obstructions to extending a homomorphism differ by minus the pulled-back difference class, and the obstructions to deforming the source with the homomorphism differ by its image under the connecting map of the transitivity triangle of the spectral nerves.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Adjoints of the degree functors on graded modules
providers.scope: The degree-n component functor on graded modules has graded coinduction as right adjoint; placing a module in degree n is right adjoint to the degree-n component after reduction modulo the positive part.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded cotangent complex
providers.scope: The graded cotangent complex forgets to the cotangent complex; its degree-zero part is the cotangent complex of the degree-zero rings, and for B^0 = A its degree-one part is B^1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded transitivity triangle
providers.scope: Maps of graded rings A -> B -> C give a distinguished triangle of graded cotangent complexes, compatible with forgetting the grading and with degree zero.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded square-zero extensions
providers.scope: Graded square-zero extensions are classified by Ext^1 of the graded cotangent complex in the derived category of graded modules, with automorphisms the graded derivations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Naturality of the Atiyah class of a module
providers.scope: The Atiyah class of a module is natural in the module and in the ring map, and vanishes for modules extended from the base by a flat module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Atiyah class through the graded cotangent complex
providers.scope: The Atiyah class of a module M is the connecting map of the degree-one part of the graded transitivity triangle of the dual numbers B + M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Principal parts and connections
providers.scope: Connections on a module correspond to splittings of its principal parts extension, whose class is the image of the Atiyah class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deformations of modules over a square-zero thickening
providers.scope: An extension of modules with prescribed action of the ideal exists exactly when an obstruction in Ext^2 vanishes; the extensions then form a torsor under Ext^1, with automorphisms Hom.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The obstruction as the product of the Atiyah class and the class of the thickening
providers.scope: The canonical obstruction class of a module over a square-zero thickening is the composite of its Atiyah class and the class of the thickening.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The universal first-order thickening
providers.scope: For the thickening A/K^2 of A/K the canonical class of a module is the class of the two-term truncation of its derived tensor product with A/K over A.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Atiyah class of an invertible module
providers.scope: On a smooth scheme the Atiyah class of an invertible module is its first Chern class in Hodge cohomology, the image of its class under dlog.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending vector bundles to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood
providers.scope: For a closed immersion of smooth schemes the obstruction to extending a vector bundle to the first infinitesimal neighbourhood is minus the boundary of its Atiyah class in the conormal sequence; on the quadric surface in P^3 over Z neither ruling line bundle extends (Example 3.11).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a morphism of modules with given source
providers.scope: Deforming the target of a morphism of modules together with the morphism is governed by the obstruction of the target and a class in a cokernel of Ext^1 groups.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The single obstruction for deforming a morphism with given source
providers.scope: Deforming the target of a morphism f_o of modules with given source is obstructed by one class in Ext^2(C(f_o), K), C(f_o) the cone of f_o; the solutions form a torsor under Ext^1(C(f_o), K) and their automorphisms are Hom(coker f_o, K).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The canonical obstruction for morphisms of modules
providers.scope: The obstruction for deforming a morphism with given source is the image of a canonical class with coefficients in a pushout, which is the composite of an Atiyah class of f_o with the class of the thickening.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded obstruction for modules and the derived tensor product
providers.scope: For the deformations of a module, the obstruction obtained from the graded transitivity triangle of the dual numbers is the canonical class of the derived tensor product; the two identifications of the torsor are inverse to each other.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived category
providers.scope: Complexes with finite filtrations up to filtered homotopy, localized at the maps that are quasi-isomorphisms on all graded pieces, form a triangulated category; a morphism is an isomorphism when its graded pieces are.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered objects and their Yoneda extensions
providers.scope: Filtered objects form the full subcategory of objects whose graded pieces have cohomology in degree 0, and their filtered Ext groups are the Yoneda extensions with exact graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived Hom
providers.scope: With enough injectives, the filtered Hom complex into a bounded below complex of injective type computes the filtered derived Hom, and its H^n F^0 is the filtered Ext group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The spectral sequence of a filtered derived Hom
providers.scope: The filtration of the derived Hom gives a convergent spectral sequence from the Ext groups of the graded pieces, whose first differential is composition with the extension classes, with explicit signs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of a tensor product
providers.scope: If one filtered complex has flat graded pieces, the graded pieces of the tensor product are the tensor products of the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The filtered derived category is symmetric monoidal
providers.scope: The derived tensor product makes the filtered derived category of a ringed topos a symmetric monoidal category, and the underlying complex and the associated graded are symmetric monoidal functors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cartan's isomorphism for filtered complexes
providers.scope: RHom(L (x) M, N) = RHom(L, RHom(M, N)) on the filtered derived category, compatibly with the associated graded; the filtered derived category is closed symmetric monoidal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived pullback and pushforward of filtered complexes
providers.scope: Derived pullback is left adjoint to derived pushforward on filtered derived categories, with the internal form RHom(L, Rf_*M) = Rf_* RHom(Lf^*L, M), compatibly with the associated graded.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Composition and product of internal Homs
providers.scope: In the filtered derived category, the composition of internal Homs is compatible with their product: the product of two composites is the composite of the products, after the symmetry.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Global composition and global product
providers.scope: The global composition of derived Hom complexes is compatible with the global product.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Duality for perfect filtered complexes
providers.scope: For filtered perfect L, the biduality morphism, the morphism from the dual tensor M to RHom(L, M) and the product of internal Homs are isomorphisms, with no boundedness condition.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Dualizable objects of the filtered derived category
providers.scope: An object of the filtered derived category has a dual exactly when its graded pieces are perfect; the dual is RHom(L, A) with evaluation and an explicit coevaluation.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Additivity of traces
providers.scope: For a filtered perfect complex E and a filtered morphism E (x) K -> E (x) L with K, L unfiltered, the trace on E is the sum of the traces on the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplicativity of traces
providers.scope: The trace of the tensor product of two morphisms of perfect filtered complexes is the tensor product of their traces, on morphisms and internally.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cup products and traces
providers.scope: The cup product of u: E (x) K1 -> F (x) L1 and v: F (x) K2 -> E (x) L2 is additive on graded pieces and multiplicative, and Tr(uv) = Tr(vu) = <u, v> for endomorphism-type pairs.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of powers of a filtered module
providers.scope: If the graded pieces of a filtered module are flat, the graded pieces of its symmetric, exterior and divided powers are the corresponding powers of its graded module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived powers of filtered and graded complexes
providers.scope: Symmetric, exterior and divided powers derive to the bounded above filtered and graded derived categories; the graded pieces of LT^n(L) are sums of derived tensor products of the LT^m(gr^i L).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Amplitude of derived powers
providers.scope: If L has tor or perfect amplitude in an interval [a,b] containing 0, then LT^n(L) has tor or perfect amplitude in [na,nb].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered Koszul sequences
providers.scope: For a sequence of filtered modules with exact flat graded pieces, the Koszul sequences are exact on every filtration step, with graded pieces the Koszul sequences of the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shift isomorphisms on filtered derived categories
providers.scope: LS^n(M[1]) = LΛ^n(M)[n] and LΛ^n(M[1]) = LΓ^n(M)[n] on the bounded above filtered and graded derived categories, with the shift formulas of complexes as underlying isomorphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Graded pieces of the shift isomorphisms
providers.scope: On graded pieces the shift isomorphisms are sums of tensor products of the shift isomorphisms of the graded pieces, composed with the isomorphisms of shifted tensor products, with the sign (-1)^(sum over i<j of n_i n_j) for the second one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagonal maps and Koszul sequences
providers.scope: The diagonal maps carry the Koszul sequence of an exact sequence tensored with M to the Koszul sequence tensored with S^n M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived diagonal maps
providers.scope: For filtered complexes concentrated in degrees at most 0: LS^n(L (x) M) -> LS^n L (x) LS^n M and LΛ^n(L (x) M) -> LΛ^n L (x) LS^n M, natural and compatible with graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Diagonal maps and shift isomorphisms
providers.scope: The diagonal maps commute with the shift isomorphisms of L (x) M and of L, for L and M concentrated in degrees at most 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Shift isomorphisms as ring isomorphisms
providers.scope: The shift isomorphisms identify Hom(A, LS(M[1])) with Hom(A, LΛ(M)[1]) as rings of series, and, after the signs (-1)^(n(n-1)/2), Hom(A, LΛ(M[1])) with Hom(A, LΓ(M)[1]).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Trace of a shifted morphism
providers.scope: For E perfect and g: E (x) K -> E (x) L, Tr(g[a]) = (-1)^a Tr(g).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: L-series on filtrations and gradings
providers.scope: The L-series of a filtered morphism E -> E (x) M is that of its graded pieces; for a graded morphism it is the product of the L-series of the components.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: L-series of a shifted morphism
providers.scope: L_t(f[1]) = L_t(f)^(-1) and L_t(f[2]) = L_t(f) for f: E -> E (x) M with E, M concentrated in degrees at most 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Characteristic series through exterior powers
providers.scope: c_t(f) = sum over n of (-1)^n Tr(psi^n LΛ^n(f)) t^n for E and M concentrated in degrees at most 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Characteristic series of maps of complexes
providers.scope: For a map of complexes phi of a strictly perfect complex, c_t of its class is the product over i of det(1 - t phi^i)^((-1)^i), which therefore depends only on the class.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered Dold-Puppe
providers.scope: Normalization identifies filtered simplicial objects of an abelian category with filtered complexes in degrees at most 0, and their localization with D^{<=0}F.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered complexes and chains
providers.scope: The filtered derived category of objects with filtration in [0,n] is equivalent to the derived category of chains of n+1 modules, with graded pieces the cones of the maps of the chain.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Filtered Atiyah class
providers.scope: A filtered complex in D^{<=0}F has an Atiyah class in DF whose underlying morphism is the Atiyah class and whose graded pieces are the Atiyah classes of the graded pieces.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Atiyah class and shifts
providers.scope: at(E[1]) = at(E)[1] for the Atiyah class written E -> E (x) L[1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Atiyah class and principal parts
providers.scope: The image of the Atiyah class in E (x) Omega[1] is the class of the sequence of principal parts of B over A tensored with E, also for filtered complexes.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplicativity of Chern classes
providers.scope: The total Chern class of a perfect complex is multiplicative on filtrations, gradings and distinguished triangles.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Base change of Chern classes
providers.scope: Chern classes are compatible with base change along squares of rings, morphisms of topoi and morphisms of ringed topoi.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The integral rank
providers.scope: Over a local ring of a topos, perfect complexes have an integral rank in Gamma(T, Z), additive on triangles; with the total Chern class it defines a homomorphism on the Grothendieck group.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Chern classes in Hodge cohomology
providers.scope: The Hodge-cohomology Chern classes are computed from the principal parts class and satisfy the Whitney formula and functoriality.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: First Chern class of an invertible module
providers.scope: For an invertible module, c'_t = 1 + c'^1 t, with c'^1 the negative of the class of the principal parts extension twisted by the dual.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first Chern class of an invertible module on a smooth scheme
providers.scope: For an invertible module on a smooth scheme, c'^1 is minus the first Chern class in Hodge cohomology defined through dlog.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cohomology on the topos of an open subset and its complement
providers.scope: On Top^o(i), R Gamma of (i^*F -> F), (G -> 0) and (0 -> F) is R Gamma(X, F), R Gamma(U, G) and R Gamma_Y(X, F), compatibly with the triangle of cohomology with supports.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Partial connections as Leibniz maps
providers.scope: Partial connections relative to 0 -> L -> Omega|_U -> M -> 0 correspond to additive maps nabla: E|_U -> M (x) E|_U with nabla(bm) = b nabla(m) + v(db) (x) m.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The localized class of a partial connection
providers.scope: The localized class at(E, D) on Top^o(i), with coefficients in (L -> Omega), restricts on X to the principal parts class of E.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Chern classes with supports
providers.scope: The Chern classes of (E, D) lift those of E; Chern polynomials of weight larger than r, with L locally a direct summand of B^r, lie in H^n_Y(X, Omega^n) and map to the Chern polynomials of E.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Bott's partial connection
providers.scope: For a locally free involutive submodule F of the tangent module, locally a direct summand on U, nabla(bar s)(xi) = bar [xi, s] is a partial connection on the normal module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Chern polynomials of the normal module of a foliation
providers.scope: Chern polynomials of weight larger than the rank of the normal module on U come from cohomology with supports in Y, and vanish when U is the whole space.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Principal parts of complex spaces
providers.scope: For a morphism of complex spaces, the principal parts of order one on the diagonal of the fibre product are the principal parts of the analytic differential; for a smooth morphism the differentials are free on the dz_k.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Chern classes of complex spaces
providers.scope: The Chern classes of a complex of bounded perfect amplitude on a complex space, in analytic Hodge cohomology, come from the analytic principal parts and satisfy the Whitney formula, functoriality and the dlog formula.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Localized classes for smooth morphisms of complex spaces
providers.scope: For a smooth morphism of complex spaces, a partial connection on an open subset localizes Chern polynomials of large weight in cohomology with supports in the complement.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Strict graded commutativity
providers.scope: In the homotopy of a simplicial ring, classes of odd degree have square zero, and a linear map M -> pi_1(R) extends uniquely to an algebra map from the exterior algebra of M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Tor algebra
providers.scope: Tor^A_*(B, B) = pi_*(P (x)_A B) is a graded ring, independent of the flat simplicial resolution, and functorial in squares of rings.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Weakly regular ideals
providers.scope: For B = A/I, theta: Lambda_B(I/I^2) -> Tor^A_*(B, B) extends the inverse of the conormal isomorphism; I is weakly regular if I/I^2 is flat and theta is an isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Koszul complex maps to Tor of the associated graded ring
providers.scope: theta extends to a homomorphism of bigraded algebras Lambda(I/I^2) (x) S(I/I^2) -> Tor^A(B, gr_I A) carrying the Koszul differential to the connecting maps.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Associated graded ring of a weakly regular ideal
providers.scope: For I weakly regular, Lambda^q(I/I^2) (x) S^n(I/I^2) = Tor^A_q(B, I^n/I^(n+1)), so S^n(I/I^2) = I^n/I^(n+1) is flat, and Tor_q(B, A/I^(k+1)) -> Tor_q(B, A/I^k) is zero for q >= 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor of the quotients by the powers of a weakly regular ideal
providers.scope: For I weakly regular and q >= 1, the Koszul terms Lambda^(q+j)(I/I^2) (x) S^(n-j)(I/I^2) resolve Tor^A_q(B, A/I^(n+1)), naturally in (A, I).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The ideal of the variables is weakly regular
providers.scope: For a flat B-module F, the ideal S^+_B(F) of S_B(F) is weakly regular.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Koszul-regular ideals are weakly regular
providers.scope: An ideal generated locally by Koszul-regular sequences is weakly regular, and I/I^2 is free on the classes of the generators.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Connectivity after base change to pi_0
providers.scope: A module with flat terms over a simplicial ring B is k-connective if its base change to pi_0(B) is.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Connectivity of Koszul terms
providers.scope: For a module V with flat terms over a simplicial ring and pi_0(V) = 0, Lambda^a V (x) S^b V is (a + b)-connective.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quillen's convergence theorem
providers.scope: If J is an ideal of a simplicial ring R with pi_0(J) = 0 and every J_n weakly regular in R_n, then J^m is m-connective for every m.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Convergence for the standard resolution
providers.scope: If B (x)_A B = B, P is the standard resolution and Q = P (x)_A B, then J^m is m-connective and pi_n(Q) = pi_n(Q/J^m) for m >= n + 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Low-degree stable homology of the free abelian group
providers.scope: For an abelian sheaf X, the stabilization of the free abelian group functor has H_2 = X/2X and H_3 = the kernel of multiplication by 2 on X, and its homology in positive degrees is torsion.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Spectra over the derived tensor product
providers.scope: Over the integers, the extension of spectra to complexes over the derived tensor product is not fully faithful: for the ring R of that lesson, Hom(R, R[4]) = 0, while the corresponding group of spectra is Z/2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The augmentation ideal of the Tor resolution
providers.scope: For B (x)_A B = B and Q = P (x)_A B, J/J^2 = L_{B/A} and J^q/J^(q+1) = S^q(L_{B/A}) as simplicial modules; pi_0(L_{B/A}) = 0, and for B = A/I, H_1(L_{B/A}) = I/I^2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The two conormal isomorphisms agree
providers.scope: For B = A/I, the isomorphism H_1(L_{B/A}) = I/I^2 through Tor^A_1(B, B) and the augmentation ideal of the Tor resolution is the one given by the naive cotangent complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Symmetric powers of 1-connective modules
providers.scope: For L with flat terms and pi_0(L) = 0 over a ring, S^k L is k-connective and products of classes of degree one give Lambda^k(pi_1 L) = pi_k(S^k L).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Comparison with the suspension of pi_1
providers.scope: If moreover pi_1(L) is flat and pi_i(L) = 0 for 2 <= i <= n, then pi_j(S^k L) = 0 for j <= n + k - 2, j != k (k >= 2); if pi_i(L) = 0 for all i >= 2, then pi_j(S^k L) = 0 for all j != k.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Multiplicative spectral sequences
providers.scope: The spectral sequence of a finite multiplicative filtration of a differential graded ring is a spectral sequence of bigraded rings, converging to the graded ring of the homology.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The fundamental spectral sequence
providers.scope: For B (x)_A B = B: E^2_(p,q) = H_(p+q)(S^q L_{B/A}) => Tor^A_(p+q)(B, B), a convergent first-quadrant spectral sequence of bigraded algebras.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Weakly regular ideals and the cotangent complex
providers.scope: For B = A/I: I is weakly regular iff D_q(B/A, M) = 0 for all M and q >= 2 iff I/I^2 is flat and L_{B/A} = (I/I^2)[1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cotangent complex of a Koszul-regular quotient
providers.scope: If I is Koszul-regular, then I/I^2 is locally free and L_{B/A} = (I/I^2)[1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor amplitude
providers.scope: Tor amplitude in a ringed topos: connective objects, base change, faithfully flat descent and extensions in triangles.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Examples of weak complete intersections
providers.scope: Algebras with L = Omega flat (polynomial algebras), quotients by weakly regular ideals, and local complete intersection homomorphisms of rings and morphisms of schemes have L of tor amplitude in [-1, 0].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Composition, cancellation and descent
providers.scope: Weak complete intersections compose; cancel against a factor with L = Omega flat; and descend along faithfully flat C when C is one over A and over B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Quotients of algebras with flat differentials
providers.scope: For P -> B surjective with kernel I and L_{P/A} = Omega_{P/A} flat, B is a weak complete intersection over A iff I is weakly regular; then L_{B/A} = (I/I^2 -> Omega_{P/A} (x) B).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor-independent base change
providers.scope: In a topos with enough points, L_{B/A} (x)^L B' = L_{B'/A'} for Tor-independent base change, and weak complete intersections are stable under it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor-independent base change in every topos
providers.scope: In every topos, L_{B/A} (x)^L B' = L_{B'/A'} for Tor-independent base change, and weak complete intersections are stable under it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Products in degree two
providers.scope: For B = A/I in a topos, H_3(L_{B/A}) -> Lambda^2(I/I^2) -> Tor_2^A(B, B) -> H_2(L_{B/A}) -> 0 is exact, the middle map being theta.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Koszul homology and the Tor algebra
providers.scope: For generators f of I, Lambda^2(B^r) -> Tor_2 -> H_1(f; A) -> B^r -> Tor_1 -> 0 is exact; if the classes of f are a basis of I/I^2 and theta_2 is surjective, f is H_1-regular.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Ext criterion
providers.scope: I/I^2 is projective and I weakly regular iff Ext^q_B(L_{B/A}, M) = 0 for all M and q >= 2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regular sequences over noetherian local rings
providers.scope: For A noetherian local and I in the maximal ideal: I is generated by a regular sequence iff I is weakly regular iff D_2(B/A, k) = 0; then every minimal set of generators is regular.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Weakly regular ideals of noetherian rings
providers.scope: For A noetherian: weakly regular = regular ideal = Koszul-regular ideal = I/I^2 projective with H_2(L) = 0 = vanishing of D_2 or Ext^2 for finite modules or of D_2 at the residue fields.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local complete intersections of finite type
providers.scope: For B of finite type over a noetherian A: lci iff weak complete intersection iff L_{B/A} perfect of tor amplitude [-1, 0] iff D_2(B/A, -) vanishes on finite modules.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Local complete intersection morphisms
providers.scope: A morphism of schemes locally of finite type over a locally noetherian base is lci iff it is a weak complete intersection.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regular immersions
providers.scope: A closed subscheme of a locally noetherian scheme is regularly immersed iff its ideal sheaf is weakly regular.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Regular local rings by the cotangent complex
providers.scope: A noetherian local ring is regular iff its maximal ideal is generated by a regular sequence iff D_2(k/A) = 0 iff L_{k/A} = (m/m^2)[1].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Presentations by regular local rings
providers.scope: For P -> C surjective with P regular local and kernel I: D_q(k/C) = D_{q-1}(C/P, k) for q >= 3, and 0 -> D_2(k/C) -> I/m_P I -> m_P/m_P^2 -> m_C/m_C^2 -> 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Complete intersections by D_3
providers.scope: A noetherian local ring is a complete intersection iff D_3(k/A) = 0 iff D_q(k/A) = 0 for q >= 3; then every presentation of the completion by a regular local ring has kernel generated by a regular sequence.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Minimal presentations
providers.scope: dim D_2(k/A) = mu(I) - edim P + edim A; presentations with I in m_P^2 exist, and for them dim D_2(k/A) is the minimal number of relations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cohomology of the arrow topos
providers.scope: For a morphism of ringed topoi f: X -> Y and C = (E <- F) in D^+(XY), restriction to Y is an isomorphism RGamma(XY, C) -> RGamma(Y, F).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived Hom out of objects over Y
providers.scope: For M in D^-(Y) and C = (E <- F) in D^+(XY): i_X^* RHom((0 <- M), C) = 0, and there are distinguished triangles i_Y^* RHom((0 <- M), C) -> RHom(M, F) -> RHom(M, Rf_*E) and RHom((0 <- M), C) -> RHom(M, F) -> RHom(Lf^*M, E).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Relative Ext groups
providers.scope: For M in D^-(Y) and F in D^+(Y) with Lf^*F in D^+(X), the relative Ext groups sit in a long exact sequence ... -> Ext^(i-1)(Lf^*M, Lf^*F) -> Ext^i(Y/X; M, F) -> Ext^i(M, F) -> Ext^i(Lf^*M, Lf^*F) -> ...
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cotangent complex of a morphism of arrow topoi
providers.scope: For a square q o f = g o p of ringed topoi and (p, q): XY -> ZT: i_X^* L_(XY/ZT) = L_(X/Z) and i_Y^* L_(XY/ZT) = L_(Y/T); likewise for (p, q): XY -> Z when q o f = p.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a morphism with its target: the general problem
providers.scope: Obstruction in Ext^2_T((0 <- L_(Y_o/Z_o)), (I <- J)) on the arrow topos of f_o, torsor under Ext^1, automorphisms Ext^0, with the long exact sequence through Ext(L_(Y_o/Z_o), J) and Ext(Lf_o^* L_(Y_o/Z_o), I).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flat deformations of a target with an extension of the morphism
providers.scope: For g_o flat and X a flat deformation of X_o over Z: obstruction in Ext^2(Y_o/X_o; L_(Y_o/Z_o), g_o^* K), torsor under Ext^1, automorphisms the derivations over Z_o into g_o^* K vanishing on X_o.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The obstruction as a product
providers.scope: The obstruction is the Kodaira-Spencer class of X_oY_o -> X_oZ_o -> S composed with the pullback of the class of the thickening XZ of X_oZ_o.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming the target first
providers.scope: The restriction of the obstruction to Y_o is the obstruction to deforming Y_o over Z; if Y_o deforms, the obstruction comes from Ext^1(Lf_o^* L_(Y_o/Z_o), h_o^* K).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending a morphism into a given deformation of the target
providers.scope: For a flat deformation Y of Y_o over Z: the obstruction o(Y) in Ext^1(Lf_o^* L_(Y_o/Z_o), h_o^* K) to extending f_o to X -> Y over Z, o(Y') - o(Y) is minus the pullback of the difference of the classes of Y' and Y, and the connecting map carries o(Y) to the obstruction of Theorem 3.2.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extending first-order operators to antiderivations
providers.scope: K-linear d_0: A -> E and d_1: E -> Lambda^2 E with the Leibniz rules extend uniquely to a K-antiderivation of degree 1 of Lambda_A E; d^2 = 0 if and only if it vanishes on A and E.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: De Rham complexes on quotients of Omega^1
providers.scope: For a surjection pi: Omega^1_(A/K) -> E with kernel N there is at most one de Rham complex with d|_A = pi o d; it exists if and only if Lambda^2 pi(d w) = 0 for w in N.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Lie algebroid of a de Rham complex
providers.scope: theta_x = [d, i_x] and [theta_x, i_y] = i_([x,y]) make E^vee a Lie algebroid over A/K when d^2 = 0; Chevalley-Eilenberg formula for d.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: De Rham complexes and Lie algebroids on locally free modules
providers.scope: For E locally free of finite type, Jacobi holds if and only if d^2 = 0 (Theorem 5.2), and de Rham complexes are anti-equivalent to Lie algebroids, the inverse given by the Chevalley-Eilenberg differential.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Invariant forms on torsors and the Atiyah sequence
providers.scope: For a torsor X -> Y under a flat group scheme over S: Omega^1_(Y/S) -> omega^1_(X/S) -> omega^1_(X/Y) -> 0 exact, the dual sequence ends with the anchor, its kernel is the Lie algebra of G_Y twisted by X through the adjoint action; exact on both sides for G smooth.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A formal category that is not strict
providers.scope: The formal additive group over a field of characteristic 0 is not isomorphic to a projective system of affine categories; in characteristic p it is one.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Divided powers extend along tensor products of augmented algebras
providers.scope: For augmented A-algebras B, C, divided powers on I_B extend to B (x)_A C without flatness; with divided powers on I_C the augmentation ideal of B (x)_A C gets a unique structure making both coprojections PD morphisms.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Divided powers on the nerve of an affine category
providers.scope: Divided powers on the augmentation ideal I of the arrows extend uniquely to every degree of the nerve; they are compatible with all cofaces exactly when the composition is a PD morphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: PD completion of a formal category
providers.scope: The completion of the nerve of an affine PD formal category along the divided powers of its augmentation ideal is the nerve of a PD-adic formal category with arrows the system of the P/I^[r], the composition induced through P/I^[2r-1]; it need not be strict.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Divided powers on arbitrary formal categories
providers.scope: For an arbitrary formal category with divided powers on the augmentation ideal of its arrows, the augmentation ideal of the nerve carries divided powers, unique up to unique isomorphism, making the factor inclusions PD morphisms; they make it a PD formal category iff the composition is a PD morphism, and its PD completion is PD-adic.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Envelopes of tensor products of augmented algebras
providers.scope: D_(B (x)_A C)(I_B (x) C + B (x) I_C) = D_B(I_B) (x)_A D_C(I_C) for augmented A-algebras; hence the envelope of the nerve of an affine category is the nerve of an affine category (Corollary 3.4), and the Čech–Alexander complex is defined.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Alexander-Whitney algebra of a cosimplicial algebra
providers.scope: The cochains of a cosimplicial algebra with d = sum (-1)^i d^i and the front-back product form a differential graded algebra; the normalized cochains form a sub-algebra.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The tensor algebra of the augmentation ideal and the normalized nerve
providers.scope: T_A(I) with the antiderivation extending d in degrees 0, 1 maps to the normalized nerve of an affine category, isomorphically in degrees <= 2, and everywhere when d^0 = d^1 on A.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The exterior derivative of a PD formal category
providers.scope: A unique antiderivation of Lambda_A(I/I^[2]) compatible with the tensor algebra; a de Rham complex when d^0 = d^1, when Omega^1 is generated by the d^0(a) - d^1(a), or when Omega^1 is flat.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Čech–Alexander complex gives the de Rham complex
providers.scope: For the Čech–Alexander complex of A/K, Omega^1 = Omega^1_(A/K) and the exterior derivative is the de Rham differential.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded ring of a flat PD formal category
providers.scope: If Omega^1_R = I/I^[2] is flat over A, Gamma_A(Omega^1_R) -> gr P is an isomorphism and the graded de Rham complex of the shifted category is the Koszul complex of the identity of Omega^1_R.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The formal Poincaré lemma
providers.scope: For flat Omega^1_R the augmented de Rham complex A -> P (x) Omega^bullet_R of the shifted category is acyclic modulo every step of the divided power filtration, hence levelwise for PD-adic R.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Cohomology of flat PD-adic formal categories
providers.scope: For a PD-adic formal category with flat Omega^1_R, affine, strict or the PD completion of one, p: N(J^[m]) -> F^m Omega_R is a quasi-isomorphism for every m: its cohomology is de Rham cohomology, with the divided power and Hodge filtrations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Invariance of the cotangent complex of simplicial rings
providers.scope: For a commutative square of simplicial rings A -> B, A' -> B' whose maps A -> A' and B -> B' are quasi-isomorphisms, L^Delta_(B/A) (x)_B B' -> L^Delta_(B'/A') is a quasi-isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Degreewise free resolutions compute the cotangent complex
providers.scope: For a map of rings A -> B and a quasi-isomorphism P -> B of simplicial A-algebras with P degreewise free, Omega^1_(P/A) (x)_P B is canonically isomorphic to L_(B/A) in D(B).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor-independent base change
providers.scope: For maps of rings A -> B, A -> A' of a topos with Tor^A_i(B, A') = 0 for i > 0, P_A(B) (x)_A A' resolves B' = B (x)_A A' by free A'-algebras and L_{B/A} (x)^L_B B' -> L_{B'/A'} is an isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cotangent complex corepresents derivations
providers.scope: Hom_(D(B))(L^Delta_(B/A), M) = Hom_(D(A-Alg/B))(B, B + M), naturally in the B-module M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The diagonal graded cotangent complex
providers.scope: For a map of graded simplicial rings, the diagonal graded cotangent complex is invariant under quasi-isomorphisms, compares with the ungraded one through theta, and its parts of degree 0 and 1 are the cotangent complex of the degree 0 rings and the corresponding degree 1 complex.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The graded transitivity triangle
providers.scope: A composite of maps of graded simplicial rings gives a graded transitivity sequence and a distinguished triangle of graded cotangent complexes, compatible with the parts of degree 0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Atiyah class of a simplicial module
providers.scope: The Atiyah class of a simplicial module M over B is the third map of the degree one part of the graded transitivity triangle of A -> B -> B + M.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Flat epimorphisms have vanishing cotangent complex
providers.scope: For a map of rings A -> B of a topos which is flat and an epimorphism of rings, in particular a localization morphism, L_(B/A) = 0 in D(B).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The cotangent complex on affine schemes
providers.scope: For a map of rings A -> B, the cotangent complex of Spec B -> Spec A is quasi-isomorphic to the quasi-coherent module associated with L_(B/A).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Tor-independent base change for ringed topoi
providers.scope: For a square of ringed topoi whose structure ring of X' is a localization of u^-1 O_X (x) f'^-1 O_S', with vanishing higher Tor, u^*L_(X/S) = L_(X'/S') and L_(X'/S) = u^*L_(X/S) + f'^*L_(S'/S).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The derived de Rham complex does not depend on the free resolution
providers.scope: For every degreewise free resolution P' -> B over A, a canonical chain of filtered quasi-isomorphisms connects L Omega_(B/A) with the realization of Omega_(P'/A), with the Hodge filtrations; gr^m = Lambda^m L_(B/A)[-m].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived de Rham complexes over rings containing Q
providers.scope: If every nonzero integer is invertible in A, then A -> L Omega_(B/A) is a quasi-isomorphism for every A-algebra B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived exterior powers of a two-term complex
providers.scope: For a map u: N -> M of flat modules, L Lambda^n(N -> M) is isomorphic to the Koszul complex of divided powers Gamma^(n-q) N (x) Lambda^q M, shifted by n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Cartier isomorphism for free algebras
providers.scope: Over a ring with p = 0, the inverse Cartier map Omega_(B^(p)/A) -> H(Omega_(B/A)) is an isomorphism of graded algebras for B free, or a symmetric algebra of a flat module.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The derived Cartier isomorphism
providers.scope: The conjugate filtration of L Omega_(B/A) has graded pieces Lambda^i L_(B^(p)/A)[-i] when Tor_j^A(B, A_F) = 0 for j > 0; in general the twisted free resolution computes them.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Derived de Rham complexes of smooth morphisms in characteristic p
providers.scope: For a smooth morphism of schemes in characteristic p, L Omega_(X/S) -> Omega_(X/S) is a quasi-isomorphism carrying the conjugate filtration to the canonical filtration.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first graded piece of the completed Čech nerve
providers.scope: For a presentation B = Q/I with Omega^1_(Q/A) flat, the normalized cochains of K/K^2 are I/I^2 -> Omega^1_(Q/A) (x)_Q B in degrees 0, 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The first graded piece for an arbitrary affine category
providers.scope: For an affine category with a surjection onto a constant algebra and flat module of differentials, the normalized first graded piece of the kernel is the two-term complex I/I^2 -> U/U^2 (x) B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Hodge-completed derived de Rham complexes of complete intersections in characteristic zero
providers.scope: Over a ring containing Q, for B = Q/I with Q weakly smooth and I weakly regular, the Hodge-completed derived de Rham complex is filtered quasi-isomorphic to the normalized Čech nerve of Q completed along the kernel to B.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Gluing monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial sets
providers.scope: A pushout of a monomorphism of simplicial sets that is a quasi-isomorphism is a quasi-isomorphism, and so is its product with a zigzag interval relative to the two ends.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Pushouts along monomorphisms preserve quasi-isomorphisms
providers.scope: A map of pushout diagrams of simplicial sets, with one leg a monomorphism in both, that is a quasi-isomorphism at each vertex induces a quasi-isomorphism of pushouts.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Left fractions in the homotopy category of simplicial sheaves
providers.scope: If the topos has enough points, the quasi-isomorphisms of simplicial sheaves form a left multiplicative system in the homotopy category.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kan's functor Ex^∞
providers.scope: For a simplicial set X, Ex^∞ X is a Kan complex and X -> Ex^∞ X is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism; Ex^∞ preserves finite limits and Kan fibrations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kan fibrations that are quasi-isomorphisms
providers.scope: A Kan fibration of simplicial sets, over any base, is a quasi-isomorphism if and only if it lifts against every monomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Anodyne extensions are the monomorphic quasi-isomorphisms
providers.scope: A monomorphism of simplicial sets is anodyne if and only if it is a quasi-isomorphism.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Kan's functor for simplicial sheaves
providers.scope: For a simplicial sheaf X, X -> Ex^∞(X) is a monomorphic quasi-isomorphism into a Kan simplicial sheaf; Ex^∞ commutes with finite limits and inverse images and preserves fibrations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Moore's theorem for simplicial groups of a topos
providers.scope: For a simplicial group G of a topos, G is Kan, pi_0 G = G_0/d_0(N_1 G) and pi_n(G) is the n-th homology sheaf of the normalized complex, abelian for n >= 1.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Fibrations of simplicial groups
providers.scope: A homomorphism of simplicial groups of a topos is a fibration iff it is an epimorphism on the normalized complexes in positive degrees, iff G -> H x_(pi_0 H) pi_0 G is an epimorphism in every degree.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Right fractions among Kan simplicial sheaves
providers.scope: If the topos has enough points, quasi-isomorphisms between Kan simplicial sheaves form a right multiplicative system in the homotopy category.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The Kan derived category is the simplicial derived category
providers.scope: For every topos, localizing the homotopy category of Kan simplicial sheaves at quasi-isomorphisms gives a category equivalent to the simplicial derived category, through Ex^∞.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Free simplicial modules on derived categories
providers.scope: If the topos has enough points, X -> Lambda^(X) induces a left adjoint of the forgetful functor D(Lambda) -> D(T) on simplicial derived categories; so Ext^p(Lambda^(X), F) = Hom_D(T)(X, sigma^p F).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups through the Hom complex
providers.scope: For a simplicial sheaf Y and a simplicial Lambda-module M, the p-th cohomology of the Hom complex of C(Lambda^(Y)) and C(M) is Hot(Y, sigma^p M).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups of free simplicial modules as colimits
providers.scope: If the topos has enough points and X is a Kan simplicial sheaf, Ext^p(Lambda^(X), F) is the colimit of H^p Hom(X', F) over the fibrant quasi-isomorphisms X' -> X.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Verdier's hypercovering theorem
providers.scope: If the topos has enough points, H^p(T, F) is the colimit of the Čech cohomology of the hypercoverings; hypercoverings are the fibrant quasi-isomorphisms to the final object (Lemma 3.4).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Giraud's theorem
providers.scope: A locally small category with finite limits, disjoint coproducts stable under pullback, effective equivalence relations with quotients stable under pullback and a small set of generators is equivalent to the sheaves on a small full subcategory of generators closed under fibre products, with the epimorphic families as coverings.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Topoi satisfy Giraud's conditions
providers.scope: The category of sheaves on a small site satisfies Giraud's conditions; so the conditions characterize topoi up to equivalence.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Second total topoi are topoi
providers.scope: For every good topos X fibred over a small category, the second total category Top^o(X) is a topos, and the level functors are inverse images of morphisms of topoi.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Classifying topoi of pseudo-categories
providers.scope: For a good pseudo-category X, the category BX of equivariant sheaves is a topos, and the nerves are inverse images of morphisms of topoi into it.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming the target of a morphism of diagrams
providers.scope: For diagrams of schemes with g_o flat and a flat deformation X of X_o over a thickening Z of Z_o: obstruction in Ext^2(Y_o/X_o; L_(Y_o/Z_o), g_o^* K) to a flat deformation of Y_o with an extension of f_o, torsor under Ext^1, automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Equivariant deformations of the target
providers.scope: For morphisms of G-schemes X -> Y -> Z with g flat and an equivariant flat deformation X' -> Z' of h = gf: obstruction, torsor and automorphisms in the relative Ext groups of the nerves N(G,X) -> N(G,Y).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a group scheme with a homomorphism from a deformed source
providers.scope: For a homomorphism u: F -> G of flat group schemes and a deformation F' of F: obstruction in Ext^2(N(G)/N(F); L_(N(G)/S), f_G^* I) to a deformation G' of G with an extension F' -> G' of u, torsor under Ext^1, automorphisms Ext^0.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Deforming a module scheme with a homomorphism from a deformed source
providers.scope: For a homomorphism u: F -> G of A-module schemes and a deformation F' of F: obstruction, torsor and automorphisms in the relative Ext groups of the spectral nerves N(A,F) -> N(A,G).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A given deformation of the target module scheme
providers.scope: If G has a deformation G', the obstruction is the image under the connecting map of the obstruction to extending u to F' -> G', which changes by minus the restriction of the difference of two deformations.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Ext groups over the ring scheme
providers.scope: For a homomorphism u: F -> G of module schemes over A_S and a deformation of F, the groups of obstruction, torsor and automorphisms are Ext groups over A_S of the cone of u with coefficients in the Lie complex of G tensored with the ideal.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
